cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Mechanical systems transmit and convert forces and motion using mechanisms such as gears, levers, cams and pulleys.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Linkages convert one type of motion to another: a bell crank converts linear motion to rotary motion; a push-pull linkage transmits motion around a corner.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Gear trains transmit rotary motion between shafts: spur gears for parallel shafts, bevel gears for perpendicular shafts, worm gears for right-angle high-ratio drives.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Gear ratio = Number of teeth on driven gear / Number of teeth on driver gear; it determines speed and torque multiplication.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Mechanical advantage (MA) = Load / Effort; velocity ratio (VR) = Distance moved by effort / Distance moved by load; efficiency = MA / VR x 100%.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Cams convert rotary motion to reciprocating (linear) motion; the cam profile determines the follower's movement pattern.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Pulleys and belt drives transmit motion between parallel shafts with flexibility and shock absorption; speed ratio = Driver diameter / Driven diameter.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Bearings reduce friction between moving parts: plain (bush) bearings for low-speed, roller/ball bearings for higher-speed applications.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Chain drives provide positive (non-slip) power transmission between parallel shafts; used in bicycles, conveyors and machinery.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Simple machines (levers, pulleys, inclined planes) provide mechanical advantage by trading distance for force.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: First-class levers have the fulcrum between load and effort (e.g. seesaw); second-class have load between fulcrum and effort (e.g. wheelbarrow).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Mechanical Systems
cards.back: Idler gears between driver and driven gears do not change the gear ratio but reverse the direction of rotation.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — mechanical systems?
cards.back: 1. For Mechanical Systems questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Mechanical Systems through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
